shots.title: THE TRAY: eyes develop
shots.text_layout: triptych: EN stack left margin, ZH vertical right margin; premise mono 0.236-1.90

text.layout: left margin x72, cap 40 px mono

shots.description: WINDOW 7:9 centred in INK. Top-down, locked: a sheet of white paper under a thin layer of developer in a black tray; the dim overhead safelight lies on the liquid as a soft grey rectangle (luminance only, no hue). Frame 0 is already this image. From 0.2356 the liquid rocks (one slow wave per 2 bars) and development starts in 16 discrete pulses on the 16th grid (0.2356 ... 1.9401): each pulse doubles the number of developed halftone dots, ordered by rate = darkness x certainty, so the pupils and irises lead, the hair mass follows as a soft cloud; by 1.1447 two eyes are readable. 2.045 "I": pupils snap to full density. 2.50 "see": irises full. 2.852 "sparks": a small VOICE-orange catchlight in each eye (the only colour inside the window, 6-frame bloom). 3.635 / 4.32 / 4.54 (A-G-I): brows and lash line; nostrils and lip line; hair mass. 4.77-5.23 "in your eyes": midtones fill outward from the eyes; the ear rims, the outer hairline and the jaw outline stay thin (density cap = certainty). 5.40: the print blinks once (stage 1: both catchlights go out for 2 frames; stage 2: P06). The print is the photograph itself (identity/face_clean_1024.png) cropped to the face: no border, no page, no passport framing, no scan line, no lift into 3D.
shots.camera: top-down, locked, FOV 16 deg vertical, print fills the 7:9 window (crop to the face: chin just above the bottom edge, no shoulders or shirt, top of the hair inside the print (never ID framing); face width ~70 % of window)

shots.text_layout: left margin stack (1:1), letter parts for C-G-P-T; ZH vertical right

THE BEAM: medium close-up, eye level, black space; he stands in a hard projector beam that comes from beside the lens (frontal, so the face is evenly lit), eyes closed, chin at most 10 deg up. The beam carries a projection of his own photograph, offset (+6 % x, -4 % y) and 10 % too large, a ghost face over his face; it slides into exact registration on "alive" (21.36): the machine's version eats his face. The four registration marks start doubled and converge on the same frame. The projector lamp flickers on the 16th hat roll (22.054-22.963). The kick drives; the image never cuts.

shots.description: Aerial, straight down: 100,000 hanging prints in rows, cold top light and the backlight glow, no per-print lamps (the memorial register is avoided). It reads as a data hall and as a silent audience. PROOF 100,000. Rendered once as a held still at 2560x1440 and panned in 2D.

shots.title: The mirror print
shots.description: Two prints of him side by side on the line: the true print, and the same negative printed emulsion-side flipped, his mirror image, the face people prefer of themselves; the reversed edge-code lettering in its border is the tell. On R, L, H and F four small grease-pencil ticks accumulate beside the mirror print (approval). On "askew" (121.83) the true print's clip lets go on one side and it hangs crooked, about 7 deg.

shots.title: Copy of a copy: until only the paper remains
shots.description: Ten generations as ten jump cuts on the 8th grid (cuts at 130.008 ... 131.827). Each cut re-photographs and re-prints the previous print of the photograph: contrast up, grain up, softer, tones flattening, halftone coarsening. At 131.599 the face is gone and only the paper and its tooth remain (Lucier: until only the room remains); the orange catchlight is the last trace and goes at 131.827. His features are never reshaped toward any other face. PROOF runs 2^n.

shots.title: What did Ilya see?
shots.text_layout: CARD "What did Ilya see?" 132.00-133.38; NONE 133.38-137.40; CARD "Was it" begins 137.40 (spans into S53)
shots.description: ONE HELD SHOT: the opening framing again, the tray from above, now 16:9. A fresh white sheet slides into the developer by itself. We wait. Nothing develops. The liquid rocks. At 133.38 the card, the subtitles and the HUD all vanish.

shots.title: The stop: everything freezes
shots.text_layout: CARD "Was it all for show?" completes word by word; ZH small beneath
shots.description: At 138.417 everything freezes: the rocking developer stops mid-wave, a drop hangs in the air above the tray. The image dims to 15 % over 4 frames while the CARD completes: "all" 138.42, "for" 139.32, "show?" 140.16; 这一切只是一场表演吗？ small beneath.

shots.title: THE WALK: the hall records him
shots.text_layout: the S53 CARD persists across the cut until "show?" ends (141.10), fading over 6 frames; then no text; HUD = PROOF counter only
shots.description: ONE SHOT: the hall at night, locked on the aisle axis with a slow zoom in. He walks at the lens at half time (heel strikes on beats 1 and 3): the only time he is present without sung words, the film's one broken rule. The rows of sheets are blank again, and they record him as he passes: 12 captures on the beats of bars 78-80 (before each capture the sheet flashes, for its beat, one image from earlier in the film, in film order), 24 on the 8ths of bars 81-83, 16 on the 16ths of bar 84. Each capture fixes a side-view silhouette of his stride on its sheet: the hall behind him fills with a Muybridge sequence of his walk. The backlight climbs from night toward white, with no bloom in the last bar. 151.145: a 2-frame full-frame capture flash, and under it the 3D silhouette hands off to plate P10 (close-up, walking into the lens). On the last beat (152.508) his face fills the frame.
